PlacementPolicy carries `backings` (src/definition/placement.ts#AuthoredCodeBackingPolicy), a partial map from the closed SPEC 4.7 consumer set to an opaque AuthoredCodeBackingId, read through backingFor(consumer, profileDefault); an unmapped consumer takes the substrate profile’s declared default and never another offered backing. The declaration is now load-bearing rather than inert, which is what moved this row off planned: C13-FACET-CODE-AVAILABILITY refuses a code- or both-available Operation at Blueprint validation when neither policies.placement nor the profile maps a backing for the programmaticToolCall consumer. That refusal is evidenced on the W4 row C13-BLUEPRINT-VALIDATE-BEFORE-LOAD, whose cited titles carry its label; this row cites its own five labelled declaration tests rather than borrowing them.

Worker Loader is the only SPEC 4.7 backing the Cloudflare package implements. It loads the isolate with `globalOutbound: null`, `disallow_importable_env`, and an `env` holding one entrypoint stub per delegated Binding and nothing else, all three exercised against real workerd in the cloudflare lane.

The former dispatch-namespace adapter was removed because it could not establish the abstract AuthoredCodeBacking contract it claimed: outbound posture is a property of the binding’s deployed outbound Worker, not of `DispatchNamespace.get()`. Restoring the SPEC 10.2 dispatch backing requires a configured deny-all outbound Worker, the exact deployed binding, and a real substrate test proving both `fetch` and `connect` are unavailable while passed Binding capabilities stay callable.

Verification stays blocked on two things this row may not supply, and the second is now named exactly rather than as a wave's debt. C13-PLACEMENT-DYNAMIC-NO-EGRESS remains an explicit prerequisite, is planned, and is W4-declarative with a W8 substrate obligation behind it, so the ledger refuses this row a promotion whatever its own evidence says. And the profile half has no implementation to integrate against: PlacementSourcePort is answered by no production subclass anywhere in either package — every implementation in the tree is a test double — so `authoredCodeBackingDefault(consumer)` has no profile answering it, while the only backing packages/agent-core-cloudflare offers is cloudflare/src/authored-code.ts#WORKER_LOADER_BACKING and no dispatch-namespace backing exists to be the second. The owed evidence is therefore a Cloudflare PlacementSourcePort that answers both of the port's members and a W8 test resolving a declared consumer to WORKER_LOADER_BACKING through it; supplying it decides the profile's per-manifest isolation-mode policy as well, which is why it is a slice of its own and not a citation this row can add.
bounds: This rule does not carry a per-consumer compute or subrequest budget, and that is now a decision rather than an open question: C13-CLOUDFLARE-DYNAMIC-COMPUTE-BOUND asked whether the consumer-to-bound mapping belongs in policies.placement beside the consumer-to-backing mapping of SPEC 9.2, and W4's answer is that it does not. What 9.2 declares is which backing serves which 4.7 consumer, through an opaque AuthoredCodeBackingId a profile resolves; a per-load CPU-time and subrequest bound is one substrate's resource vocabulary (cloudflare/src/loader.ts#DynamicWorkerLimits mirrors workerd's own limits) with no substrate-neutral unit, and PlacementSourcePort declares only substrateModes and authoredCodeBackingDefault because a Blueprint validated before any package code loads cannot check a bound it has no units for. The bound therefore belongs where the backing is constructed, and a profile wanting different budgets per consumer constructs one adapter per budget. Reopening this means giving the definition plane a substrate-neutral resource unit first.

W4's definition plane selects the mode and constructs no domain, so no W4 symbol can witness a refused connection and no substrate-neutral interface, nominal token, or local reference can stand in for one.

The rule is not closeable by any single substrate's evidence either: one backing demonstrating zero ambient egress says nothing about another, so this is a rule about what every backing must preserve rather than a claim any one of them discharges. The substrate obligation is C13-CLOUDFLARE-DYNAMIC-NO-EGRESS (W8, §10.2): adversarial code in a real isolate failing both global fetch and connect while an explicitly passed Binding stays callable.
